agree.reason: A free 20-minute call is easy to say yes to, and the plain, honest tone builds trust, but she pays her cousin $600 a year and this costs $2,388, and nothing on the page tells her why paying the difference is worth it.

honest.reason: The facts are reported faithfully and the missed deadlines and price rise are disclosed openly, but 'One of them saved $800' states as fact what was only the client's own report, and 'Clients stay until they sell' stretches a one-year sample of two departures.

works_the_facts.reason: Figures are restated rather than worked out: there is no annual cost ($2,388), no retention rate (29 of 31), no on-time rate (9 of 12 closes), and the $800 saving is never set against the price.

right_comparison.reason: The page never describes this reader's real alternative, a relative doing the books once a year at tax time, or what monthly books give her that a year-end catch-up doesn't.

qualification.reason: The hedge on monthly closes gives a date she can check (the 10th) and a count (missed three times last year), but it never says what happens to her when a close is late.

objections.reason: Her main objection, cost and loyalty compared with her $600 cousin, is never met, while the space goes on the phone hours and the price-rise history, which matter less to her.

fit.reason: It runs to roughly 330 words of sales-page copy with clear sections and ends on the booking button, as the brief asked.
